thread:
alex_support: Hey team — customer on a private VPC reporting intermittent failures when our on-prem agent pulls models/artifacts. Error is TLS verify failed + `certificate subjectAltName mismatch`. Happens ~1-2x/day for different model pulls. No proxy logs show blocked IPs. Can we get a concise egress host list and any special TLS/OCSP endpoints they must allow?

maria_network: Thanks, Alex. Quick question: are they terminating TLS (TLS interception) in their proxy or doing SNI passthrough? TLS interception will cause SAN mismatches.

alex_support: They said corporate proxy does TLS MITM for inspection. We suspect that but errors mention `requested hostname model-registry.redwood-ai.com`. Example client log: `curl: (60) SSL: certificate subject name '*.artifactory.internal' does not match 'model-registry.redwood-ai.com'`.

tim_oncall: If they're MITMing, they need to either 1) exempt our hosts from interception (SNI passthrough) or 2) install their trusted CA on the host where the agent runs. But we should give them all hosts to exempt. Also check OCSP/CRL — MITM often breaks stapling.

jenna_eng: I'm pasting a minimal allowlist we recommend for private installs — note there are both public CDN endpoints and internal registry endpoints (split DNS). They need both DNS names and wildcard patterns. Please share this with their network team.

jenna_eng: ```
Required outbound hosts (HTTPS/TCP 443):
- model-registry.redwood-ai.com
- registry.prod.redwood-inference.com
- shards-*.models.redwood-ai.com  (wildcard)
- packages.redwood-inference.net (PyPI/apt proxies)
- apt.storage.redwood-inference.net
- artifacts.redwood-inference.com (artifactory)
- telemetry.redwood-inference.com
- auth.redwood-inference.com (OAuth/JWKS)
- oauth-idp.redwood-inference.com
- registry-cdn.redwood-cdn.com
- s3.eu-central-1.amazonaws.com (for model shards pulled from S3)
- container-registry.redwood-inference.com

Also allow OCSP/CRL endpoints and PKI services used by our CA (TCP 80/443):
- ocsp.redwood-inference.com
- crl.redwood-inference.com

KMS & license checks (if using Private integrations):
- kms.eu1.redwood-sec.com:443

DNS & discovery: ensure DNS resolution for the above names returns both internal IPs (for VPC/private routes) and public IPs as needed. If they have split-horizon DNS, ensure internal ranges are reachable.```

alex_support: This is perfect — thanks. Can you also add any IP ranges? They asked for IP ranges to add to the firewall.

jenna_eng: We don't publish stable IPs for CDN-backed hosts because they change. For infra endpoints (ocsp, crl, auth, telemetry) we can provide ASN-backed prefixes: allow outbound to AWS prefixes in eu-central-1 and us-east-1, and our Cloudflare ASN for CDN. If they must use IPs, they should allow the domain names and update their allowlist automation. I'll add a note: wildcard DNS is required for shards.

maria_network: Also call out DNS over TCP/UDP and DoT (port 853) if they route DNS through a recursive resolver that might split. If the resolver can't reach public DNS for our CDN entries, split-horizon can return private IPs that don't route to the agent. Quick repro steps for them:

maria_network: ```
# from the host where agent runs
# verify cert chain and SNI
openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood-ai.com:443 -servername model-registry.redwood-ai.com -showcerts
# check OCSP stapling
openssl s_client -connect model-registry.redwood-ai.com:443 -status -servername model-registry.redwood-ai.com
# verify DNS resolution
dig +short model-registry.redwood-ai.com
# if result is private IP, ensure private route exists; if public IP, ensure firewall allows outbound
```

tim_oncall: If they see `subjectAltName mismatch` with MITM, the short-term action is to exempt the domain from interception. Long-term we can support a configuration where agent ignores MITM if an internal CA is installed, but that's riskier. For now ask them to allowlist the FQDNs in the proxy.

alex_support: I'll send their network team the list. One more: customer reported intermittent `x509: certificate signed by unknown authority` specifically for `packages.redwood-inference.net`. Is that likely OCSP or CDN edge?

jenna_eng: Could be their proxy replacing certs without installing the proxy CA in the container/agent runtime. Also check that `packages.redwood-inference.net` resolves to our CDN (Cloudflare). If their resolver is returning an internal IP, that can return a different cert.

ops-bot: Ticket created: #INC-2026-451 (linked to customer ticket 98765). Assigned to @alex_support. ETA: 48h for network team review. :white_check_mark:

maria_network: One additional note — allow outbound to the following for telemetry and probe uploads (port 443): `telemetry.redwood-inference.com` and `metrics-ingest.redwood-inference.net`. If they do strict proxy auth, ensure the agent's service account/token is allowed and not stripped by the proxy.

alex_support: Thanks all — I'll follow up with the customer with these steps + the openssl/dig commands and ask them to either exempt the hostnames or provide proxy CA to the agent. I'll update the ticket when I hear back. :thumbsup:
